context: Theorem 10 (Main Result) Let c ∈ (0, 1/2) be any constant and η0 = 1/2 − c. Then, there is an algorithm that testably learns the class Hhs with respect to EXMassart Massart N ,Hhs ,η0 = {EXN ,f,η : f ∈ Hhs , supx∈Rd η(x) ≤ η0 } with time and sample complexity poly(d, 1/ϵ) log(1/δ). Moreover, even if the input set S̄ is arbitrary (not necessarily i.i.d.), upon acceptance, the algorithm outputs h ∈ Hhs s.t. P(x,y)∼S̄ [y ̸= h(x)] ≤ optS̄ + ϵ , where optS̄ = minf ∈Hhs P(x,y)∼S̄ [y ̸= f (x)]. The final part of Theorem 10 states that the guarantee we achieve is actually stronger than the one in Definition 3, since the output is near-optimal whenever the algorithm accepts, without requiring that the input S̄ consists of independent examples. For small c, the runtime of our algorithm scales as (d/ϵ)poly(1/c) . This gives a polynomial-time algorithm when c is constant, but we leave it as an interesting open question whether the dependence on 1/c can be improved. We provide lower bounds for the case c = 0 in Section F. The proof of Theorem 10 follows the same outline we provided for the case of random classification noise. However, there are two differences. First, we need a version of Fact 9 that works under Massart noise (and Gaussian marginal) and gives an algorithm that approximately recovers the parameters of the ground truth. Second, the disagreement tester from before does not give a testable bound for the quantity |S̄b |/|S̄| = P(x,y)∼S̄ [y ̸= sign(v · x) and sign(v∗ · x) ̸= sign(v · x)] 12
